solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Early Pope permits one to misbehave

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in line, so the words permits one are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old pontiff lets someone behave badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to misbehave' rearranges the ten letters of PERMITS ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Simon Peter is held by Catholic tradition to have been the first Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Only bloke without a po?

definitions.note: po is short for po-faced, an adjective meaning humourless and disapproving

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor

indicators.note: without says the following letter is taken away from the word for bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: is a man without a chamber pot the only one?
explanation.walkthrough: PO is British slang for a chamber pot, which the surface leans on; as the definition it is a clipped form of 'po-faced'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone po-faced wears a grave, unsmiling expression, so the shortened form stands as a synonym.

clue.text: Millions readily shunned by one of miserable attitude

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

indicators.note: shunned by tells us the letter for one is cast out of the word for readily

parts.note: readily means easily
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited person happily turns down millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly describes something contemptibly small or mean, matching a miserable, grudging disposition.

clue.text: Worked meaner land than earlier people

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters are kneaded or reshaped like soil, signalling an anagram of the following words

explanation.surface: Ancient farmers tilled poorer ground than those who came before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked' rearranges MEANER LAND THAN.
explanation.definitionFit: These hominids lived before modern humans, an extinct species that preceded us.

clue.text: One exploits Queen engaged in duty with King

indicators.note: with here means alongside, so the King's letter is added after the rest
engaged in means held inside, so the Queen's letters sit within the word for duty

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
R, Rex, is the King

explanation.surface: Royalty taking part in a tax arrangement exploits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One exploits' means one who exploits, in the sense of putting to use or exercising.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it fully, so a person who does that is an exploiter of it.

clue.text: Top part of converted prison not completed

parts.note: something converted is no longer what it was, a former thing, hence EX

indicators.note: not completed means the final letter is left off

parts.note: a cell is a prison

explanation.surface: The upper floor of a jail turned into flats is unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: A converted prison is an EX-CELL; 'not completed' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo or surpass, a verb sense of top.

clue.text: Substantial reversal of power in French company

indicators.note: reversal of says the assembled letters are read backwards
in places the letter for power inside the French company abbreviation

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A big change of control inside a French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside CIE to give CIPE, which 'reversal of' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a grand, heroic scale is very large and imposing, so substantial.

clue.text: Mountain climbing a boost, sidelining thoughts of sex?

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
a tonic is a boost or pick-me-up

explanation.surface: Mountaineering as a pick-me-up that keeps the mind off sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic love is affectionate friendship free of sexual desire, after Plato's ideal.

clue.text: Cunningly, airmen landed upside-down within country's borders

indicators.note: within places the airmen and landed pieces between the border letters
borders are the outer letters, the first and last of the word country's

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are airmen

indicators.note: in a down clue upside-down means read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: lit is landed, as a bird lit on a branch

explanation.surface: Pilots crashed and landed upside down inside a country's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landed' is LIT, as a bird lights on a branch; 'country's borders' are its first and last letters, C and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning or wily, and this is its adverb form.

clue.text: Hold suggestion after party receives cash

indicators.note: after puts the suggestion word following the party word

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: receives says the cash letters are taken inside

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle suggestion or shade of meaning
tin is slang for money, cash

explanation.surface: A tip-off that a party takes money is put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' looks like a verb but is a noun, a halt; 'receives' places the cash inside the party-plus-suggestion string, not inside the party alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold is a pause or stop, and a discontinuance is a stopping or suspension.

clue.text: Source of wool providing turnover for a lot of shops

indicators.note: turnover suggests flipping, so the words a and the shopping centre are read backwards

parts.note: a mall is a collection of shops

explanation.surface: Wool supply provides the business takings of many shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like retail income but reverses A MALL.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American camelid is shorn for its fleece, so it is an example of a wool supplier.

clue.text: Exotic lunch idea not for everyone — a Mexican dish

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearrangement
not for means the letter standing for everyone is removed

parts.note: U, the universal film certificate, means suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: An unusual lunch suggestion that not everyone would like: a Mexican dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not for' removes U (universal: for everyone) from LUNCH IDEA, and 'Exotic' rearranges the rest; A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rolled tortilla with filling and chilli sauce, a food from Mexico.

clue.text: Describing air? Oxygen in mix, I start to concede

indicators.note: in places the oxygen symbol inside the word for mix

parts.note: to meld is to blend or mix
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of concede

explanation.surface: Someone stirring oxygen into a mixture, about to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' here is a tune, not the atmosphere that 'Oxygen' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and a melodic piece is tuneful, so the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Rugby player not selected when hands don't work?

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
out means omitted or not picked for the team

explanation.surface: A rugby forward dropped from the side when his hands fail him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' are workers, not the fumbling fingers of a player.
explanation.definitionFit: In this dispute an employer bars staff from the workplace, so the workforce cannot do their jobs.

clue.text: Leader's power, dealing with occupation

definitions.note: a possessive noun here, standing for an adjective meaning belonging to a leader

parts.note: residential relates to living in, occupying, homes

explanation.surface: A ruler's authority in handling a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' suggests a job, but here it means living in a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to a head of state, such as a palace or a jet, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Slate data storage — accessed it, but article's missing

parts.note: a disc stores computer data

indicators.note: missing says the article is taken out

parts.note: data is read when it is accessed
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A disk was hacked and an article lost, and critics condemn it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to criticise harshly, and to discredit is to damage a reputation, a close sense.

clue.text: Soprano with little energy intermittently interrupting weak stringed instrument

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the word for weak
intermittently says the soprano and energy letters break in at separate points rather than together

parts.note: paltry means feeble or weak
E is the abbreviation for energy, a little of it

explanation.surface: A singer with little vigour now and then breaking into a feeble song on a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently interrupting' puts S and E into PALTRY at two places: P-S-ALT-E-RY.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient instrument has strings plucked over a flat soundboard, like a zither.

clue.text: Hard when you first vote to ignore one European increase

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: to ignore says the letter for one European is passed over

parts.note: eighteen is the voting age in the UK
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: It's tough, at first voting, to overlook a European and boost things.
explanation.walkthrough: The age of first voting is EIGHTEEN; dropping one E gives EIGHTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to make higher or more intense, so it is a synonym of raise.

clue.text: He prepares dish without a recipe at first, cooking common meal

indicators.note: cooking says the letters are worked over into something new
at first takes the opening letter of recipe

explanation.surface: A cook makes a homely dish without a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A and R (recipe at first) from HE PREPARES DISH, and 'cooking' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This minced lamb and mashed potato pie is a familiar everyday British dinner.

clue.text: Hunter turned in — lot of beds knocked over

indicators.note: turned means the word in is read backwards
knocked over in a down clue means upended, so reversed

parts.note: a dorm, dormitory, is a room with many beds

explanation.surface: A hunter went to bed after a row of beds toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimrod is the 'mighty hunter' of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible calls him a mighty hunter, so the name became a byword for a skilled huntsman.

clue.text: Induced to include information in story

indicators.note: to include says the information letters go inside

parts.note: led means induced or persuaded
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Persuaded to put facts in a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale, often of uncertain truth, so a kind of story.

clue.text: Cricketer supports barracking?

parts.note: legs are supports, as for a table
lip is impudent talk, like the jeering of barracking

explanation.surface: A cricket player backs the jeering from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg slip is a fielding position close behind the batter on the leg side; the term also names the fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder stationed in that cricket position is often called by its name, so it names a player.

clue.text: Muscle guy going topless is a nut

parts.note: pec, short for pectoral, is a chest muscle

indicators.note: going topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A muscular man stripping to the waist is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like a madman in the surface, but defines the food.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the edible kernel of a North American hickory tree, a kind of nut.

clue.text: Course that's retained in procedure

indicators.note: that's retained says the following word is kept inside the course word

parts.note: a route is a course or way

explanation.surface: A course of action kept within standard procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, regular way of doing things, a set procedure.

clue.text: Transported — via Gate 4?

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet, so gate 4 can be gate D

explanation.surface: An airline passenger sent off through Gate 4.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests travel, but means delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away by emotion, enchanted or delighted.

clue.text: At no time run two steps forward, showing self-possession

indicators.note: two steps forward says the run letter moves two places toward the front of the word

parts.note: never means at no time
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Never running, but taking two steps forward with composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is courage or cool composure, the steadiness of self-possession.

clue.text: American recalled no end of funk

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse
end of takes the last letter of funk

parts.note: nay means no

explanation.surface: A US citizen remembered no final panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses K + NAY (no).
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal for someone from the United States.

clue.text: Inclined to follow tuna at sea, with no-one in support

indicators.note: to follow puts the inclined word after the tuna letters
at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters of tuna are mixed

parts.note: tended means inclined, as in tended to agree

explanation.surface: Tuna swimming at sea alone, with no others accompanying them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' makes UNAT from TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattended means left alone, without anyone present to help or watch over.
